name: org.openrewrite.apache.httpclient4.MigrateDefaultHttpClient
description:
Since `DefaultHttpClient` is deprecated, we need to change it to the `CloseableHttpClient`. It only covers the default scenario with no custom `HttpParams` or `ConnectionManager`.

Of note: the `DefaultHttpClient` [does not support TLS 1.2](https://find-sec-bugs.github.io/bugs.htm#DEFAULT_HTTP_CLIENT).

References:

description: Adds a `// TODO Ignite 3` comment above each statement that uses an Ignite 2 API which Ignite 3 removed, or replaced with something that cannot be derived from the call alone: starting an embedded node, creating caches on demand, compute closures, data streamers, services and data structures, cache queries, binary objects, iterating over a cache and the other cache operations that `KeyValueView` does not have, and the transaction APIs beyond beginning, committing and rolling back. name: org.openrewrite.apache.ignite.MigrateCacheToKeyValueView
displayName: Migrate Ignite 2 caches to Ignite 3 `KeyValueView` tables
description: Ignite 3 replaces caches with tables. A cache obtained with `cache(name)` or `getOrCreateCache(name)` becomes `tables().table(IgniteNameUtils.quoteIfNeeded(name)).keyValueView(K.class, V.class)`, which reads the table that the Ignite 3 migration tools create for that cache. The key-value operations of `IgniteCache` and `ClientCache` move to `KeyValueView`, taking the transaction as their first argument: the enclosing Ignite 2 transaction where there is one, and `null` otherwise, which runs the operation in an implicit transaction of its own. A lambda or anonymous class inside a transaction gets a comment unless it is passed to a `java.util` method that runs it on the same thread. `getAllOutTx` becomes `getAll` outside any transaction. `containsKey` becomes `contains`, `containsKeys` becomes `containsAll`, and `clear` becomes `removeAll`. Operations without an Ignite 3 equivalent, such as `size`, `query` and `invoke`, are left as they are. A lookup with `getOrCreateCache` gets a comment, since the table has to be created before it can be read.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating from [Apache Ignite](https://ignite.apache.org/) 2.x to 3.x.
category3Description: Recipes to perform [Apache](https://apache.org/) project migration tasks.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.ignite.MigrateThinClientConfiguration
displayName: Migrate the Ignite 2 thin client configuration to `IgniteClient.builder()`
description: Ignite 3 builds a thin client with `IgniteClient.builder()` instead of starting one from a `ClientConfiguration` with `Ignition.startClient`. The addresses, the address finder, the user name and password, the heartbeat interval, the async continuation executor and the built-in retry policies move to the builder; the timeout becomes both the connect and the operation timeout, as it was used for both in Ignite 2; partition awareness is dropped, as Ignite 3 always uses it. Note that Ignite 3 retries only reads by default, where Ignite 2 retried every operation. A configuration that sets anything else, uses an address with a port range, or is built where this recipe cannot follow it, is left as it is with a comment.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating from [Apache Ignite](https://ignite.apache.org/) 2.x to 3.x.
category3Description: Recipes to perform [Apache](https://apache.org/) project migration tasks.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.ignite.MigrateTransactions
description: Ignite 3 transactions are begun with `IgniteTransactions.begin()`, are not `AutoCloseable`, and are not bound to the thread. A try-with-resources over `txStart()` becomes a transaction begun before a try block that rolls it back in its `finally` block, which does nothing once the transaction has committed, as `close()` did in Ignite 2. Ignite 3 has no concurrency or isolation modes, so those arguments are dropped; a timeout becomes `TransactionOptions.timeoutMillis`. Where the transaction is in scope of a call that may have run in it implicitly, such as a method of the application, a comment says that the operations meant to run in it now need it as an argument.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating from [Apache Ignite](https://ignite.apache.org/) 2.x to 3.x.
category3Description: Recipes to perform [Apache](https://apache.org/) project migration tasks.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.ignite.RemoveRedundantCatchAlternatives
displayName: Remove catch alternatives that Ignite 3 merged
description: Ignite 3 throws `IgniteException` where Ignite 2 threw `ClientException` or `IgniteException`, so a multi-catch of both names one type twice once the types are changed, which does not compile. This keeps the first of them, and drops an alternative that is a subclass of another, such as `IgniteClientConnectionException` next to `IgniteException`.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating from [Apache Ignite](https://ignite.apache.org/) 2.x to 3.x.
category3Description: Recipes to perform [Apache](https://apache.org/) project migration tasks.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.ignite.UpgradeApacheIgniteDependencies_3
description: Replaces `ignite-core` with the Ignite 3 thin client, `ignite-client`. The `ignite-core` artifact of Ignite 3 holds internal classes only, so its version is never just upgraded. Ignite 3 builds SQL in and configures nodes with HOCON, so `ignite-indexing`, `ignite-calcite` and `ignite-spring` are removed, and so are the Ignite 2 logging adapters. A module that used Ignite only through one of those modules gets `ignite-client` added. Applications that embed an Ignite 3 node need `ignite-runner` and `ignite-api` instead.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating from [Apache Ignite](https://ignite.apache.org/) 2.x to 3.x.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.ignite.UpgradeApacheIgnite_3
description: Migrates Apache Ignite 2.x applications to the Apache Ignite 3.x client API. Caches become tables read through a `KeyValueView`, transactions are passed explicitly to the operations that run in them, the thin client is built with `IgniteClient.builder()`, and the build moves from `ignite-core` to `ignite-client`. Ignite 3 removes much of the Ignite 2 API, among it cache and node configuration in Java, compute closures, data streamers, services and the embedded node started with `Ignition`; each statement using these is left in place with a `// TODO Ignite 3` comment that says what replaces it. A statement that passes a cache to a library built for Ignite 2, such as a rate limiter, gets such a comment too.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.httpclient5.MigrateHttpStatusConstantsInterface
description: HttpClient 4's `org.apache.http.HttpStatus` is an interface of constants, while HttpClient 5's `org.apache.hc.core5.http.HttpStatus` is a final class. Remove `HttpStatus` from `implements` (and from an interface's `extends`), and qualify the `SC_*` constants that were inherited through it as `HttpStatus.SC_*`.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating to [Apache HttpClient 5.x](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-client-5.4.x/).
category3Description: Recipes to perform [Apache](https://apache.org/) project migration tasks.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.httpclient5.RemoveSettingsIgnoredWithConnectionManager
displayName: Remove `HttpClientBuilder` connection settings ignored next to `setConnectionManager`
description: HttpClient 4's `HttpClientBuilder` applies `setDefaultSocketConfig`, `setDefaultConnectionConfig`, `setMaxConnTotal`, `setMaxConnPerRoute`, `setConnectionTimeToLive` and `setDnsResolver` only to the connection manager it creates itself, so they have no effect when the same builder chain also calls `setConnectionManager`. HttpClient 5's `HttpClientBuilder` no longer has these methods; remove them from such chains.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating to [Apache HttpClient 5.x](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-client-5.4.x/).
category3Description: Recipes to perform [Apache](https://apache.org/) project migration tasks.

name: org.openrewrite.apache.httpclient5.MigrateUrlEncodedFormEntityStringCharset
displayName: Replace `new UrlEncodedFormEntity(List, String)` with `new UrlEncodedFormEntity(Iterable, Charset)`
description: HttpClient 5's `UrlEncodedFormEntity` takes the charset as a `Charset` only. Replace a supported charset name literal with the `StandardCharsets` constant, or with `Charset.forName(..)`, and a `static final` `String` constant declared in the same file with `Charset.forName(CONSTANT)`. Other arguments, which may be `null`, are left for manual migration.
category2Description: Recipes for migrating to [Apache HttpClient 5.x](https://hc.apache.org/httpcomponents-client-5.4.x/).
category3Description: Recipes to perform [Apache](https://apache.org/) project migration tasks.
